title: Fortnightly impact log + micro-OKRs (Sam Choi)
content:
Purpose / framing:
This is my personal 2-week impact log and micro-OKR scratchpad. Not a polished update for anyone else — meant to capture reality, decisions, and quick hypotheses so I can iterate on where I spend time.

Background context (short):
- Role: platform infra, focus on autoscaling heuristics + cost/perf tradeoffs for dedicated pools.
- Problem: latency SLOs occasionally breached during mid-day bursts; cost creeping up due to overprovisioning for tail.
- Goal: reduce token-cost by 12% on our medium-throughput batch profile while keeping 95th latency within 1.2x baseline.

Micro-OKRs for next 2 weeks (concrete + measurable):
1) Objective: Reduce batch token cost for medium queue
   - KR1: Implement KV-prefix caching experiment (A/B) on 2 routes; measure per-token CPU/GPU time change 
     Baseline: 1.00 token-GPU-ms / token (est)
     Target: -12%
   - KR2: Tune batching policy to reduce redundant small-batches >= 20% of calls without raising p95 > 1.2x
2) Objective: Shorten investigation-to-fix cycle time for SLO incidents
   - KR1: Create 2 runbook templates + sample tracing links that shave avg incident TTR by 25%
   - KR2: Run 1 dry-run incident postmortem with on-call to validate runbook

Key metrics (current snapshot + how I calculate):
- Medium-profile token cost: $0.0026 / token (avg last 30d)
- 95th latency (medium): 780ms (baseline window 30d)
- Cache hit-rate (prefix KV): 0% (feature not yet in prod)
- Batch occupancy: 0.42 (ratio of live tokens per batch / max batch capacity)

Measurement notes (for my future self):
- token-cost calc = (gpu_charge + infra_charge + amortized infra) / tokens_generated_in_window; use billing export table + request logs join on deployment_id. SQL stub below (quick sketch):
  SELECT deployment_id, SUM(gpu_seconds * gpu_price) / SUM(tokens) AS token_cost FROM billing_samples WHERE window = '30d' GROUP BY deployment_id;
- Latency p95 derived from request_latency_ms histogram; need to exclude truncated/abandoned requests (status != "abandoned").

Two-week plan (day-level rough):
Week 1:
- Mon: prototype prefix-KV layer in local runtime; end-of-day microbench
- Tue: integrate toggles + telemetry for cache hits, misses, evictions; basic dashboard
- Wed: small-scale A/B (canary) on staging; collect perf/gpu metrics
- Thu: review canary with Lina; adjust eviction policy; patch on PR #412
- Fri: retrospective note + sync with on-call to draft runbook
Week 2:
- Mon: rollout A/B to 10% traffic for medium-profile; watch p95/gpu usage closely
- Tue: collect 48h data; analyze token-cost delta and p95 shift
- Wed: if safe, increase to 50% OR revert; dry-run incident with on-call for runbook validation
- Thu: finalize PR, doc runbook to Confluence, update linked artifacts
- Fri: write this log + summary email (if good results)

Early hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Prefix-level KV caching will reduce repeated KV recompute across similar prompts by ~10-18% in medium-profile.
- H2: Current batching policy is tuned for average throughput, so bursts create many small batches — increasing the batching wait threshold by 8ms will improve occupancy without harming p95 for >95% of requests.
- H3 (risk): Caching will increase tail latency for cold-vs-warm keys due to eviction churn — need eviction policy tuned to TTL and request frequency.

Experiments to run / success criteria:
- Exp A: KV prefix on medium-profile, 50% traffic for 72 hours. Success = token-cost drop >= 10% AND p95 <= 1.2x baseline.
- Exp B: Batching wait + small jitter, canary 20%. Success = batch occupancy >= 0.6 AND no >3% increase in 95th latency.

Blockers / open questions:
- Q1: Can we access token-level billing join reliably for shorter windows? (ask finance for access to new billing export table)
- Q2: Are there legal concerns with caching prefixes for customer data? Need security review (Lina flagged).
- Q3: Who owns fallback policy if A/B causes regressions? Need explicit on-call step in runbook.

Quick wins I want to remember:
- Add a lightweight "latency-safe" flag to toggle batching aggressiveness per-deployment so we can try bold settings without full rollout risk.
- Precompute eviction-weight using sliding-window frequency instead of simple LRU for short-lived workloads.

Retrospective template (for after experiment):
- What happened (short): 
- Why (root cause):
- What we learned (data points):
- Next action (owner + ETA):
- If reverted, what fallback was used and why:

Personal time allocation (approx):
- 50% hands-on infra changes (code + benching)
- 20% telemetry and dashboarding + analysis
- 15% runbook / incident dry-run coordination
- 15% writeups / doc / knowledge transfer

Notes to self / raw brain dump (scratch):
- Keep PRs small -> easier to revert. 1 feature toggle per PR.
- For canaries, have automatic rollback when p95 > baseline*1.2 for 5 consecutive minutes.
- Check GCP quota for scaling test next Thursday (maybe need quota bump).
- There was a Slack thread #medium-batching on Sep 5 where Marcus posted a helpful chart — copy that into confluence.

Stuff to follow up (actionable):
- [ ] Ping finance for billing export access (Sam) -> JIRA-1245 created
- [ ] Security quick review on prefix caching (assign Lina) -> blocked until Sep 18
- [ ] Add runbook template to confluence + link in this doc (Aisha helps)
- [ ] Small perf bench infra: add microbench harness to infra repo, PR #412

Wrapping note: keep this iterative. If the A/B goes well we scale slowly and tie a postmortem to every rollout step. If it regresses — prefer fast rollback and more instrumentation rather than immediate micro-optimizations.

End of note.

Revision history:
- 2024-09-12 created (initial plan)
- 2024-09-18 added measurement SQL sketch + updated KRs after chat with Lina
- 2024-10-01 updated blockers and action items after security sync
